To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the relationship between the IC and innovation is not linear; 2) IC is not a simple sum of intangible assets; 3) IC is not the same as knowledge; 4) IC is not only a measure for the company value creation; 5) IC can be used to support innovation policies; 6) IC can be measured and reported in different ways; and 7) IC is not an easy concept to measure.
The IC of a company is an important driver of innovation.

IC and innovation are closely related, and that the IC literature has not yet sufficiently addressed the issue of how IC contributes towards corporate value creation processes and how IC can be used as an instrument to support regional innovation policies.
